sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a Passaic house?
sections.html:
Selling for cash as the house stands is usually the shortest path, since it drops repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval. A listing or private sale takes longer, yet every route has to clear the city's occupancy certificate and fire certification before closing.

Passaic is dense, and many buildings hold more than one unit. Census Bureau data shows owners living in just 23.8 percent of homes, so sellers here are often landlords, heirs, or owners of condos and co-ops. Whichever you are, sort out these items first:

  • The deed and the block and lot numbers, which every city application asks for.
  • Tenant leases and rent rolls, if any unit is occupied.
  • Mortgage payoff figures and any open municipal charges.
  • The name the buyer will take title in, because Passaic issues the occupancy certificate under the buyer's name.

sections.h2: What should I know about Passaic as a place to sell?
sections.html:
Passaic sits on the west bank of the Passaic River, 10 miles from New York City and 12 miles from Newark Airport. It covers 3.13 square miles of land, with 71,337 residents counted in the 2025 estimate, about 22,500 for every square mile. Clifton wraps around it on the north, south and west, and six bridges carry traffic across the river toward Wallington, Garfield and Rutherford.

Dutch traders settled the area in 1679 under the name Acquackanonk, and the city and river take their name from a Lenape word often read as valley or place where the land splits. It became an independent village in 1871 and was chartered as a city in April 1873, growing into a textile and metalworking center. Main Avenue follows the river from Passaic Park to downtown, and Broadway crosses the city east to west. Passaic Park is known for its large park and larger homes in Queen Anne and Tudor styles, along with condominium towers and garden co-ops.

Industry shaped the street grid. The Okonite company ran its wire plant here from 1878 to 1993, supplying insulated cable for early telegraph lines and for Thomas Edison's first generating station in Lower Manhattan, and 36,000 mill workers walked out in the 1926 textile strike. Experimental television broadcasts began from the city in 1931. Condominium and co-op owners in Passaic Park, in complexes such as the 21-floor Carlton Tower and the post-war Barry Gardens garden apartments, should ask their association what documents a buyer needs. Passaic Park today holds an Orthodox Jewish community of more than 1,300 families, with over 20 yeshivas and other institutions and many kosher food shops, and Main Avenue reflects a growing Latino population. The city's inspection steps below apply to every sale, whoever the buyer is.

The Passaic City School District runs 17 schools and enrolled about 14,500 students in 2018-19, and Passaic County Community College opened a campus in the city in 2008. Route 21 is the main road, and the Passaic rail station on NJ Transit's Main Line serves Hoboken and Secaucus Junction. Local and Port Authority buses stop at the Passaic Bus Terminal, and jitneys run along Main Avenue.

Renters outnumber owners about three to one here, and households are large. The table lists Census Bureau QuickFacts figures for the whole city.

About 94 percent of residents had not moved in the past year, and 72.3 percent use another language at home. Bilingual listing and closing documents can help buyers follow the paperwork, and the city's own occupancy forms list inspection reports as emailed to both parties.

sections.h2: What does the City of Passaic require before a sale?
sections.html:
A sale in Passaic needs two approvals: an occupancy certificate, and a smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification. The one-family application, filed with the Division of Housing under Inspections and Code, asks for the seller's details and the buyer's name, because the certificate is issued to the buyer. Companies buying through an LLC or corporation must supply the registered agent and the certificate of formation.

  • Certificate fee: $65 on the one-family application, with an expedite option at $300.
  • Inspection and violation reports are emailed to both seller and buyer, and extra copies require an OPRA request.
  • Fire Prevention charges $45 for the first smoke and carbon monoxide inspection and $25 for a reinspection.
  • The fire certification stays valid for three months and covers only the buyer named on it.

The fire inspector looks for a smoke detector on each level, detectors and a carbon monoxide alarm outside every sleeping area, working units, and a fire extinguisher within ten feet of the kitchen. A 90-day temporary certification is available when items fail. The city notes that the occupancy certificate says the property meets Passaic's zoning and property maintenance laws and does not replace construction permits or health approvals. Condo, one, two and three family homes all use the fire form.

sections.h2: What state fees and forms apply to a Passaic sale?
sections.html:
The state's Realty Transfer Fee lands on the seller at recording. A home valued at the Census median of $429,900 lands above the $350,000 line, where the rate starts at $2.90 per $500 of price. Sales at or below $350,000 pay $2.00, $3.35 or $3.90 per $500 in steps. Passaic sellers who inherit a house from a parent, or who deed to a child, usually qualify for an exemption, which is claimed on a notarized Form RTF-1 recorded with the deed.

The GIT/REP form rides along with the deed as well, telling the State whether a seller living out of state must prepay income tax. Whoever signs the deed completes it.

Flood disclosure has been mandatory since March 20, 2024. Passaic is hemmed in by the river on one side, so look up the FEMA zone for your lot with the DEP Flood Risk Notification Tool and answer the disclosure statement questions before the buyer is bound.

sections.h2: How are Passaic property taxes appealed?
sections.html:
An owner who thinks the city's figure is too high files Form A-1 with the Passaic County Board of Taxation. The board must have it by April 1, or by May 1 where Passaic has carried out a revaluation or reassessment.

Proof is on the owner: the assessment must be shown unreasonable against market value or the district's common level range. Anything assessed above $1,000,000 can go straight to the State Tax Court, and a county board decision can be carried to that court within 45 days. The city tax collector can supply your balance and open charges.

faqs.q: Whose name goes on the Passaic occupancy certificate?
faqs.a: The buyer's. The city's one-family application says it issues the certificate under the buyer's name, and an LLC buyer must supply its registered agent and certificate of formation.

faqs.q: What does the Passaic occupancy certificate cost?
faqs.a: The one-family application lists a $65 certificate fee, plus a $300 expedite charge if you need faster handling.

faqs.q: How long does the fire certification last?
faqs.a: Three months from approval, and only for the person named on it. When the inspection finds problems, a 90-day temporary certification can be issued.

faqs.q: Does the seller cover the state transfer fee in Passaic?
faqs.a: Yes. The State bills the seller at recording, and the fee steps up with the sale price.

faqs.q: Where does a Passaic owner take an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: To the Passaic County Board of Taxation, by April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation. Owners above $1,000,000 in assessed value may skip ahead to Tax Court.
